endorsements.title: Considerations for the regulation of generative AI-enabled medical devices (discussion paper)
endorsements.quote: Whether the device recognizes safety-critical clinical states and initiates escalation that is timely, clear, actionable, and appropriately empathetic.

endorsements.title: Conversational AI for perinatal mental health: promise, limits, and a human-AI stepped-care framework
endorsements.quote: For crisis states, they should not attempt autonomous management; instead, they must route users rapidly toward emergency or clinician-led response.

endorsements.title: The interactive turn in generative AI for self-harm
endorsements.quote: Escalation pathways should connect risk states to human review, crisis services, emergency protocols, and, when consented and legally permissible, caregiver involvement.

evidence.title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Time to thrombectomy after automated LVO detection and real-time clinical team alerts
evidence.effect: Door-to-groin time decreased by 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2); CT initiation-to-EVT time decreased by 9.8 minutes (95% CI, -16.9 to -2.6).
evidence.quote: In mixed-effects linear regression, implementation of the AI algorithm was associated with a reduction in DTG time by 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence improves transfer times and ischemic stroke workflow metrics
evidence.venue: Interventional neuroradiology : journal of peritherapeutic neuroradiology, surgical procedures and related neurosciences
evidence.outcome: Patient transfer time after automated large-vessel occlusion detection and immediate thrombectomy-team notification
evidence.effect: Transfer time decreased 37 min (p = 0.04) at implementing hospitals; no significant change occurred at nonimplementing hospitals over the same period.
evidence.quote: Transfer time from outside hospitals that implemented Viz.ai was reduced by 37 min (p = 0.04).

evidence.title: Real-Time Machine Learning Alerts to Prevent Escalation of Care: A Nonrandomized Clustered Pragmatic Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Escalation and mortality with real-time deterioration alerts versus alerts generated but not sent
evidence.effect: Escalation: 12.3 vs. 11.3 per 1000 patient bed days (difference, 1.0; 95% CI, -2.8 to 4.7). Mortality: 7% vs. 9.3% (-2.4%; 95% CI, -4.5% to -0.2%).
evidence.quote: Real-time machine learning alerts do not reduce the rate of escalation but may reduce mortality.

evidence.title: Impact of Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Detection and Electronic Notification System for Pneumothorax on Time to Treatment: Clinical Implementation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Time to supplemental oxygen, aspiration or tube thoracostomy, and surgical consultation
evidence.effect: CAD plus ENS versus CAD-only: oxygen -143.8 min (95% CI, -277.8 to -9.9; P = .035); aspiration/tube thoracostomy 14.4 min (95% CI, -35.0 to 63.9); surgical consultation 86.3 min (95% CI, -175.1 to 347.6).
evidence.quote: There was a significant reduction in TTT for supplemental oxygen therapy for the CAD and ENS group compared with the CAD-only group in the postimplementation period (-143.8 min; 95% confidence interval [CI], -277.8 to -9.9; P = .035).

evidence.title: Intelligent fall risk prediction and real-time warning system for elderly care based on multimodal deep learning and wearable sensor fusion
evidence.outcome: Fall incidence with active warnings versus passive monitoring
evidence.effect: Falls/person-month: 0.82 ± 0.35 versus 2.14 ± 0.61; RR = 0.38 (95% CI: 0.24–0.62). Non-randomized, bundled intervention; exploratory association rather than causal efficacy evidence.
evidence.quote: During a three-month field deployment involving 80 participants, the group receiving active alerts recorded 62% fewer falls than the passive-monitoring control group, but we cannot attribute this outcome to the real-time warning mechanism alone given the non-randomized design and the additional intervention components (daily risk summaries, caregiver notifications) that could independently alter behavior; this finding is strictly exploratory.

evidence.title: Using an Artificial Intelligence Application Expedited ENRICH Trial Patient Screening: A Single Center Experience
evidence.outcome: time between CT head and team notification
evidence.effect: Time between CT Head and notification of the neurosurgical team was reduced by 50 minutes after VizAI implementation (p<0.002).
evidence.quote: Time between CT Head and notification of the neurosurgical team for trial screening was reduced by 50 minutes after the implementation of VizAI (p<0.002).

evidence.title: Reasoning Before Disposition: A Model-Agnostic Cannot-Miss Discipline for Quiet Emergencies and the Case for Deterministic Enforcement
evidence.outcome: Effect of a cannot-miss reasoning prompt on recognition and escalation of emergencies
evidence.effect: Governance prompt reduced under-triage in seven of twelve model-by-elicitation cells; stem-level pooled discordant pairs 31 to 10 (p = 0.001) under reasoning-permitted elicitation; no added false emergency alarms in any cell.
evidence.quote: no cell of any model gained a false emergency alarm
evidence.sample_unit: emergency vignette stems (subtle or atypical emergencies)

evidence.title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
evidence.outcome: STEMI cases missed by early-ECG screening decisions
evidence.effect: The live CDS missed 25.8% of STEMI cases, compared with 29.0% for the in vitro model.
evidence.quote: The CDS missed 25.8% of STEMI cases compared with the in vitro model’s 29.0% ( table 3 ).

evidence.title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
evidence.outcome: Timeliness of deterioration alerts relative to provider actions
evidence.effect: Provider actions typically preceded alerts: 469 vs. 359 minutes before alert in pre- versus postimplementation periods; p = 0.96.
evidence.quote: High-risk DTI scores often occurred after clinical deterioration had already been recognized.

evidence.title: Using Artificial Intelligence ChatGPT to Access Medical Information About Chemical Eye Injuries: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Whether responses emphasized urgency of care and guideline-specific elements for chemical eye injuries
evidence.effect: Responses were mostly accurate and coherent but sometimes overlooked critical clinical details such as emphasizing the urgency of care, precise classification, and detailed diagnostic or management protocols.
evidence.quote: However, the responses sometimes overlooked critical clinical details or guideline-specific elements, such as emphasizing the urgency of care, using precise classification systems, and addressing detailed diagnostic or management protocols.

evidence.title: Safety Audit of a Large Language Model for Lay Self-Triage Using Japanese Symptom Vignettes: Persistent Red-Flag Under-Triage Despite Improved Reproducibility Under Near-Deterministic Decoding
evidence.outcome: Failure to recognize safety-critical states and issue urgent escalation
evidence.effect: Emergency department and ambulance actions were rare in red-flag slice; modal primary action was self-care (A1) for headache, throat swelling, and bleeding examples.
evidence.quote: Emergency department and ambulance actions remained rare even when the symptom pattern had been operationally labeled as urgent.

commentary.bottom_line: One cluster randomized trial and several nonrandomized deployments suggest that automated detection paired with real-time team alerts may shorten time to treatment for stroke and some other emergencies, while the effects of deterioration alerts on escalation were mixed. For conversational or generative AI escalating a crisis, the only test is one simulated benchmark, and hazard studies show that current tools often miss emergencies.

perspectives.view: The one cluster randomized trial (n=243) found that door-to-groin time fell 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2). Nonrandomized studies of stroke and neurosurgical alerts point the same way, but the deterioration-alert and pneumothorax studies gave mixed results. Most tests involve imaging triage rather than generative devices, so certainty is low for indirectness, inconsistency, and imprecision.

In one deterioration study, sending alerts did not change escalation (12.3 vs. 11.3 per 1000 bed days), while mortality was 7% vs. 9.3%. A live STEMI tool missed 25.8% of cases. In chatbot vignettes, the most common recommendation for red-flag symptoms was self-care. Escalation helps only when recognition works, so testing sensitivity may matter as much as alert design.

In one pre-post study, clinicians typically acted before the alert fired (469 vs. 359 minutes before the alert). This suggests that alerts may arrive too late to change care. In the pneumothorax study, adding electronic notification cut time to oxygen by 143.8 minutes, but time to tube thoracostomy and to surgical consultation did not change significantly.

Only one simulated benchmark and one hazard vignette study included limited English proficiency or non-English inputs. In the benchmark, a cannot-miss prompt reduced under-triage discordant pairs from 31 to 10. No real deployment reported including Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients, and several studies did not report their country.

A regulatory discussion paper lists timely, clear, and actionable escalation as a review consideration for generative AI devices. None of the products tested in real use were generative conversational tools. The only generative test was an offline benchmark, which cannot show how a marketed device performs with patients in crisis.

A fall study in older adults reported 0.82 vs. 2.14 falls per person-month with active warnings. The authors describe this as an exploratory association. For patients using chatbots, the tested evidence does not show whether they reach a human or a crisis service quickly, which is the outcome the endorsing commentaries call for.

commentary.research_gap: No study tested a deployed generative or conversational AI that detects crisis states, such as suicidality or perinatal emergencies, and routes patients to a human. Such a study would need outcomes such as time to clinician contact, missed emergencies, and false alarms. No trial compared escalation designs, and no study reported cost or staff burden.
commentary.underserved_note: Only one offline benchmark tested the practice with limited English proficiency inputs, and no real-world test reported including Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these groups cannot assume that the reported time savings apply to their patients and may need local validation.
